persona: PE-1 graduate or early career, drawing on study, volunteer or part-time work
job_label: Graduate Administrative Assistant (part-time), Northbridge Department for Regional Services
statement: Responsible for processing incoming correspondence and grant enquiries for the regional funding team, with a focus on keeping response times quick. Helped the team work faster by staying on top of the shared inbox and making sure nothing was left waiting too long.

persona: PE-1 graduate or early career, drawing on study, volunteer or part-time work
job_label: Healthcare Assistant (part-time, while studying) – Riverside Community Clinic
statement: While working part-time on the outpatient reception desk, I redesigned the paper sign-in process into a simple colour-coded triage sheet so nurses could see at a glance which patients needed observations first. After the clinic adopted it across both morning sessions, waiting times dropped noticeably and the nurse manager asked me to train two new starters on using it.

persona: PE-1 graduate or early career, drawing on study, volunteer or part-time work
job_label: Part-time Warehouse Operations Assistant, Northgate Freight Solutions
statement: Over 10 weeks, I cut the depot's monthly spend on replacement packaging from about £1,850 to £1,210 (roughly 35%, measured against the supplier's monthly invoices). I did it by logging every damaged carton for three weeks, and the log showed that most of the damage came from one oversized box size. I then proposed switching to two smaller stock sizes, and the shift manager approved the change. I chose to trial the switch on a single loading bay first so I could check damage rates before the depot reordered stock, and the trial bay's damaged-carton count fell from 42 to 15 per month.

persona: PE-2 mid-career professional, 5 to 15 years in
job_label: Regional Inventory Planning Manager, Harbourline Home Stores
statement: Over two quarters I cut the stockout rate on our 1,200 fastest-selling SKUs across 38 stores from 9.4% to 3.1%, measured from the weekly lost-sales report. I rebuilt the reorder points around 13 weeks of point-of-sale data rather than the annual forecast because seasonal lines were reordering too late, and I chose to accept 4% higher safety stock on the top 200 SKUs only, rather than across the range, so that overall inventory value rose by just 1.2%. The two store-ops analysts on my team ran the weekly exception checks, and I made the final reorder calls.

persona: PE-2 mid-career professional, 5 to 15 years in
job_label: Senior Software Engineering Manager, Halvercrest Systems
statement: Responsible for managing a team of 12 backend engineers across the payments and billing platform, overseeing sprint planning, code review standards and on-call rotations. Worked closely with product and QA to ensure high-quality releases and drive continuous improvement across the engineering lifecycle.

job_label: Chief Growth Officer, Northbridge Learning Group
statement: Over 18 months I grew annual adult-learning enrolment revenue at our 14-campus vocational college group from £6.2m to £9.1m (audited year-end accounts) by deciding to cut three low-demand evening programmes and redirect their £400k marketing budget into employer-sponsored apprenticeships, where our regional data showed waiting lists. I personally negotiated the first eight corporate training contracts, then handed account management to a four-person partnerships team I hired. I kept curriculum design with the academic directors so quality approvals were not delayed.

persona: PE-2 mid-career professional, 5 to 15 years in
job_label: Customer Care Manager, residential new-build developer
statement: At Harrowgate Homes I took over the post-completion snagging process after repeated buyer complaints about slow defect repairs, and I introduced a single handover checklist and a 48-hour callback rule for every new homeowner. Customer satisfaction scores on our annual buyer survey improved noticeably and the number of complaints escalated to the regional director fell over the following year.

job_label: Contract Health & Safety Officer, Riverside Community Food Network (short-term engagements)
statement: Responsible for health and safety compliance across warehouse and volunteer distribution sites on a series of short contracts. Duties included conducting risk assessments, maintaining incident logs and ensuring volunteers followed manual handling and food hygiene procedures. Worked closely with site coordinators to support a strong safety culture and keep the organisation compliant with regulatory requirements.

job_label: Regional Director of Operations, Harbourline Hotels Group
statement: Was in charge of running 9 hotels across the north region and all the GMs reported to me. Looked after budgets, guest complaints, staffing and making sure brand standards were kept up, and did a lot of site visits. We worked hard to improve the guest experience and the team culture was much better while I was there.

Brought in on a 10-week engagement at Northmoor Gas Processing to review compressor maintenance scheduling, I rebuilt the planned-outage calendar around vendor parts lead times and handed it over to the site reliability team. This reduced unplanned compressor downtime and saved the client around £240,000 in avoided production losses.

On a 12-week contract at Halvorsen Castings, I replaced the night shift's paper handover log with a 10-minute standing huddle that I ran myself for the first four weeks, because the exit interviews I reviewed named confusing handovers as the main reason operators left. I then coached two shift leads to run it after I rolled off, while the plant manager kept all rota decisions. According to HR's leaver report, voluntary turnover on that shift fell from 9 of 42 operators in the quarter before I arrived to 3 of 44 during the engagement, and the pulse-survey score for 'I know what is expected of me on shift' rose from 2.9 to 3.8 out of 5.

persona: PE-5 career changer moving between industries
job_label: Casework Officer, Department for Regional Services (moving from hospitality operations)
statement: Responsible for processing incoming correspondence and casework queries within the department's service standards, drawing on a fast-paced hospitality background to keep things moving. Helped the team work through backlogs during busy periods and known for a quick turnaround on requests.

persona: PE-5 career changer moving between industries
job_label: Patient Flow Coordinator (formerly Logistics Operations Supervisor), Riverbend Community Hospital
statement: Drawing on my warehouse logistics background, I redesigned the discharge handover process on a 28-bed medical ward, replacing paper checklists with a shared digital tracker that pharmacy, transport and nursing could all update. Bed turnaround times dropped noticeably after the change, and the ward manager later asked me to roll the tracker out to two neighbouring wards.

persona: PE-5 career changer moving between industries
job_label: Operations Analyst (career changer from hospitality procurement), Northgate Freight Solutions
statement: Within my first six months at Northgate Freight Solutions, I cut monthly pallet-wrap and dunnage spend at our regional cross-dock from £18,400 to £12,900 (about 30%, tracked in our procurement ledger) by applying the supplier-consolidation approach I had used in hotel purchasing. I audited three months of invoices, found we were buying from five vendors at different unit prices, and chose to renegotiate with two of them on a volume commitment rather than switch to a cheaper film that the warehouse lead warned would raise load-damage claims. The team handled the day-to-day ordering; I owned the analysis, the vendor negotiations and the monthly cost report to the site manager.
